verdicts.trueWording: conversations only when a massive event occurs; choppiness in dialoguing
verdicts.note: Raw page read (bookanalysis.com, 200). Claim carried an empty quote field, so graded on substance: the 'Dialogues' section reads 'Most storylines in the novel employ conversations only when a massive event occurs' and 'The novel's writing style also contributes to the choppiness in dialoguing.' Page hedges with 'Most storylines'; the claim generalises to all conversations. Choppiness is attributed to the writing style rather than caused by the event-gating, but the reviewer does report a choppy dialogue texture.

verdicts.trueWording: history book, written in the style of a history book
verdicts.note: Raw page read (cannonballread.com, 200). Quote 'written in the style of a history book' appears word for word: 'It is a history book, written in the style of a history book, from the POV of a Maester in-world.' 'no storyline to speak of' is also verbatim later ('a 706 page hardcover with pretty small print, with no storyline to speak of'). Chapter-pacing limb supported: 'this is not a book meant to be read all in one go. I opted to read it in short bursts, usually a chapter or two at a time... It worked out very well.' Byline narfna, January 29, 2019, matches.

verdicts.trueWording: no overarching plotlines, little dialogue; densely researched non-fiction
verdicts.note: Raw page read (bookshelffantasies.com, 200). Sentence on page: 'reading it definitely feels like reading a densely researched piece of non-fiction. There are no overarching plotlines, and little in the way of dialogue or character development.' Quote 'little in the way of dialogue' verbatim; every limb supported. Byline Lisa @ Bookshelf Fantasies.

verdicts.trueWording: once I got into the rhythm, it took less time than imagined
verdicts.note: Raw page read (bookshelffantasies.com, 200). 'While I sometimes felt like I'd be reading this book FOREVER, once I got into the rhythm of it, it didn't take me nearly as long as I'd imagined.' Quote verbatim; 'reads faster than expected' is exactly the page's 'didn't take me nearly as long as I'd imagined'.

verdicts.trueWording: dry omniscient narrator, no personal thoughts or motives, basic reports
verdicts.note: Raw page read (thecosmiccircus.com, 200; byline Luna Gauthier, August 14, 2022). 'The book never takes on a character narrator, only a dry, omniscient narrator... it does all this without any personal thoughts or motives from the characters, just basic reports of their actions.' Quote verbatim. Inner-feelings limb supported separately: 'no character's inner thoughts and feelings are revealed.'

verdicts.trueWording: Long lists of lords and knights dominated the pages
verdicts.note: Raw page read (thecosmiccircus.com, 200). 'Long lists of lords and knights, where they were from, and how many and what type of troops they brought with them dominated the pages.' Quote verbatim. Bloat limb supported by the same review: 'it gets lost under the suffocating weight of unnecessary filler' and 'when a book is bloated with unnecessary details'.

verdicts.trueWording: how much of Mushroom can be relied on is up for debate
verdicts.note: Raw page read (blastfromthepastshelf.substack.com, 200; dated Nov 20, 2025). 'How much of Mushroom's account can be relied on is up for debate, but there's no denying that he brings these stories to life more than almost anyone else.' Quote 'up for debate' verbatim; both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: legends, myths and historical records woven together; a Westerosi textbook
verdicts.note: Raw page read; the given URL (2026/06/12) 301-redirects to booksofbrilliance.com/2026/08/08/book-review-fire-and-blood/ (200), matching the claim's 8 Aug 2026 date. 'The format allows Martin to cover centuries of events while introducing dozens of memorable figures. It feels like reading a collection of legends, myths, and historical records all woven together into one fascinating narrative.' Quote 'an actual textbook from Westeros' verbatim earlier in the piece.

verdicts.trueWording: written by a maester with only in-world knowledge, could be wrong
verdicts.note: Live euronews.com returned HTTP 406 to curl with a browser UA; recovered via Wayback raw capture https://web.archive.org/web/20250815172325id_/<url> (200). Page: 'She explained in a May 2014 video with Garcia... that "the book is written by a maester..., he has only in-world knowledge of things so he could be wrong on some points and chose to leave some things out".' Quote verbatim; 'She' is Antonsson (the video is hers with Garcia, and Garcia is named separately), so the attribution limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: offering explanations before dismissing one as silly, or mischievously skipping
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture of the euronews page. Attributed on the page to Reddit user feldman10, who claimed early access: 'Elio and Linda, writing as Maester Yandel, clearly have a lot of fun with the material, often offering several potential explanations for mysterious or disputed events before dismissing one as silly, or mischievously skipping over material they can't reveal by claiming it must be already well-known to the reader.' Quote 'mischievously skipping over material' verbatim; 'a reader' matches the page's redditor-with-early-access.

verdicts.trueWording: the maester is forced to walk a careful line for Great House descendants
verdicts.note: Raw page read (drunkmonkeys.us, 200; Donald McCarthy). Quote 'forced to walk a careful line' is verbatim: 'the founders of many of the Great Houses in Westeros were not exactly the most honorable of warriors... since the maester is writing for the descendants of those Great Houses, he is forced to walk a careful line.' Graded SUBSTANCE rather than VERBATIM because the page never uses the name 'Yandel' (0 occurrences); it says only 'the maester'/'a maester'. Substance of the claim is fully supported.

verdicts.trueWording: not a surprise he calls it 'The Glorious Reign', complicating reliability
verdicts.note: Raw page read (drunkmonkeys.us, 200). 'House Baratheon is in control and it's therefore not a surprise that the maester refers to his reign as "The Glorious Reign," further complicating how reliable we should take the text when it discusses the history of the Baratheons and their allies.' Quote verbatim. The page does not use the word 'bias', and says 'his reign' under Baratheon rule rather than naming Robert; both limbs are nonetheless directly supported by 'therefore not a surprise' plus the reliability clause.

verdicts.trueWording: impossible to fully know all events; some records contradict one another
verdicts.note: Raw page read (drunkmonkeys.us, 200). 'The maester writing admits that it is impossible to fully know all historical events and that some records contradict one another and he therefore gives us both. There are certain events that appear concrete, but some are still ambiguous enough to keep us wondering.' Quote verbatim; every limb, including the ambiguity limb, supported.

verdicts.trueWording: not an easy read, basically as a textbook, you plough through it
verdicts.note: Raw page read (litcritpop.com, 200). 'It is not an easy read, as it is basically as a textbook. You really do have to be interested in Westeros in order to plough through it.' Quote 'basically as a textbook' verbatim; the ploughing limb is the page's own next sentence (conditioned on being interested in Westeros).

verdicts.trueWording: point of view moving around a large rep company, most afraid
verdicts.note: Raw page read (lrb.co.uk, 200; masthead confirms John Lanchester, 'When did you get hooked?', Vol. 35 No. 7, 11 April 2013). 'The books tell this story by hopping about from person to person across the wide geography of Westeros and beyond, with the point of view moving around a large rep company of principal characters, most of them, most of the time, afraid for their lives.' Quote verbatim; every limb supported ('rep company' = repertory company).
